site.line: Web apps I build for myself and a few people around me. Everything below runs on this server.
site.sub: Public ones work for anyone. Sign-in ones show a sign-in screen to visitors.
site.footer: Every app is TypeScript, mostly a React client on a Fastify and SQLite API, deployed from one repo. The source of most of them is on GitHub.

sections.title: Games and toys
sections.line: Play in the browser, no account needed.

cards.name: Games portal
cards.blurb: The four games on one page, each playable in its own frame.
cards.more: All four run on one deterministic TypeScript engine, so any run replays exactly from its seed. Pick a game and it opens on its own page.

cards.name: Farm Valley
cards.blurb: 21 farmers compete for gold on a ring of islands, and you mostly watch.
cards.more: A simulation server runs the farmers and the browser draws them in WebGL2. A panel on the right lists the farmers and what each one is doing.

cards.name: Citadel
cards.blurb: A settlement builder: lay roads, place houses, keep the town fed.
cards.more: Start from one road, add houses, a well, a chapel and a market, then speed the days up and deal with what each day brings.

cards.name: Hollow
cards.blurb: A society across generations, in 3D, with charts of who lives and dies.
cards.more: Hollow follows a town's families over decades. The chronicle on the left logs the town's events as they happen, beside charts of the population.

cards.name: MateQuest
cards.blurb: A math roguelike: answer the sum and your knight lands the hit.
cards.more: Pick a fight on the map and solve arithmetic to attack. The problems and buttons are in Romanian.

cards.name: Solstice
cards.blurb: Model a house and its plot, then see it under the real sun on any date.
cards.more: A browser editor and path tracer. Set a place and a date and the light falls where it really would. This copy has no server, so Save downloads the scene file.

sections.title: Apps for home
sections.line: Used every day by me and a few people. Visitors see the sign-in screen.

cards.name: ImbatranimOS
cards.blurb: Alpine Linux in a container, used through a Windows 7-style desktop in the browser.
cards.more: It has one owner, so a visitor sees only the sign-in screen. Its office suite, games and tools install from its Marketplace. The README starts your own copy with Docker Compose.

cards.name: Atrium
cards.blurb: One household's books, music and video, with notebooks and LaTeX beside them.
cards.more: A library on its own server. Read, listen and watch in one place, and keep notes and LaTeX documents next to the books they are about.

cards.name: Shelfmark
cards.blurb: A catalog of the paper books at home. Scan a barcode and it is listed.
cards.more: Scan with the phone camera and the details fill in. The list sorts, filters and exports to Excel or CSV.

cards.name: Almanac
cards.blurb: A calendar that works like Google Calendar, private for each user.
cards.more: Day, week, month and year views, repeating events, and a calendar of your own that nobody else sees.

cards.name: Lantern
cards.blurb: Rate films and series, keep a watchlist and get suggestions.
cards.more: Each suggestion names the title you liked that put it there. Film data comes from OMDb and IMDb's public data files.

cards.name: sports-app
cards.blurb: A calisthenics trainer for beginners at home. It picks today's session.
cards.more: No equipment needed. It plans the month, tracks progress against targets and opens offline once you have signed in.

cards.name: Satchel
cards.blurb: A small messenger for a few friends, with an ideas inbox.
cards.more: Group chats for a handful of people. Claude Code reads the ideas inbox from the command line, so an idea typed on the phone becomes work later.

cards.name: Postern
cards.blurb: Gmail-style webmail for this server's own mail.
cards.more: It talks JMAP to the Stalwart mail server. Conversations, labels and folders work the way they do in Gmail.

cards.name: newspapper
cards.blurb: Write Instagram news posts in a small markup and export the slides.
cards.more: Type the post on the left and the 1080 by 1080 slides update as you write. Export them as JPEGs.

cards.name: ro-housing
cards.blurb: A flat hunt in Timișoara: nine listing sites in one table.
cards.more: Listings arrive with their price history, prices per square metre sit beside them, and a shortlist keeps the ones worth a visit.

sections.title: Sites for other people
sections.line: Websites made for small businesses, a parish and friends. Most are in Romanian.

cards.name: Trips
cards.blurb: Week-long trips from Timișoara, planned day by day for a small group.
cards.more: Each destination has a day-by-day plan, a map, the costs, a reading guide and a printable poster.

cards.name: Ana Saloon
cards.blurb: A nail salon in Târgu-Jiu: services, prices and WhatsApp booking.
cards.more: A static Astro site in Romanian. Prices start at 80 lei and the booking button opens WhatsApp.

cards.name: BavAuto Gorj
cards.blurb: A BMW repair garage in Târgu-Jiu, with call and WhatsApp buttons.
cards.more: A static Astro site in Romanian. It lists the common faults the garage fixes, with a call button up front.

cards.name: AXA Tractări
cards.blurb: A demo site for car towing in Oltenia, phone lines first.
cards.more: A static Astro site in Romanian. Three phone lines sit at the top, because that is what someone stuck on the road needs.

cards.name: Subcort
cards.blurb: A demo site for event tent rental in Gorj, by tent size.
cards.more: A static Astro site in Romanian, with the tent sizes on offer.

cards.name: Churchix
cards.blurb: A platform for parish sites, shown with one Orthodox parish.
cards.more: A white-label platform for Orthodox parish sites. The home page leads with the next service and this week's schedule.

cards.name: Fourteen Renderings
cards.blurb: One blog drawn in 14 different design styles.
cards.more: The same blog, rendered fourteen times, from Minimalism and Swiss Design to Brutalism, to compare how type, colour and layout change one page.

cards.name: CivicMap
cards.blurb: Parks, libraries, clinics and museums in Timișoara and București, with what is on.
cards.more: A proof of concept: the places are real and the events are made up. Filter by kind of place and see the week's listings.

cards.name: Mercatus
cards.blurb: A demo marketplace for digital files, priced in lei.
cards.more: Templates, fonts, graphics and e-books with e-Factura invoices. Browsing is open and payments are simulated.

sections.title: Behind the scenes
sections.line: What keeps the apps running. Most of it is for me only.

cards.name: Ward
cards.blurb: The shared sign-in. One account, and a grant per app decides who gets in.
cards.more: Most apps offer Sign in with Ward next to their own accounts. Ward is an OpenID Connect provider with a console for apps and grants.

cards.name: Wicket
cards.blurb: One queue for every LLM call the apps make, served in ticket order.
cards.more: It holds the model key and runs one call at a time, so no app needs a key of its own.

cards.name: brief-board
cards.blurb: Where every planned change stands across all the projects.
cards.more: A Jira-style board of every brief, with what is waiting on me at the top.

cards.name: Status
cards.blurb: Every public address on this server, checked once a minute.
cards.more: A Gatus dashboard. Green means the address answered in the last minute.

cards.name: just-a-bot
cards.blurb: A Discord bot for one server: play-money casino, party games, a text RPG.
cards.more: It has no public invite, so its docs are what you can open here.

cards.name: Grafana
cards.blurb: Charts of the server: requests, memory, containers.
cards.more: Prometheus collects the numbers and Grafana draws them.

cards.name: Vault
cards.blurb: The password vault, a Vaultwarden server.
cards.more: Bitwarden apps on the phone and laptop sync to it.

cards.name: Mail
cards.blurb: The mail server's admin, a Stalwart server.
cards.more: Postern reads the mail. This is where the accounts and domains are set up.

sections.title: On GitHub
sections.line: Projects that don't run on this server. Each card opens its repo.

cards.name: imbatranim-apps
cards.blurb: Docs, Sheets, Slides, PDF and CAD apps for ImbatranimOS.
cards.more: They install from the OS's Marketplace and run only inside it, so the repo is where you can see them.

cards.name: my-personal-skills
cards.blurb: The Claude Code skills that run every project here: wiki, briefs, design and review.
cards.more: Each project keeps a corpus wiki and written briefs. These skills plan, split and review the work.

cards.name: SocialEvents
cards.blurb: A planner for a company's social events, on a calendar and a map.
cards.more: Invite people or whole departments, see the weather at each place, and rate events afterwards. Runs locally only.

cards.name: hackathons
cards.blurb: Three hackathon projects, among them Nutrisha, an AI meal planner from ITFest.
cards.more: Also an API uptime dashboard and a WhatsApp chat analyser. Several earlier repos merged into one, with their history kept.

cards.name: mini-projects
cards.blurb: Five small tools: a diff viewer, a password manager, a TSP solver and more.
cards.more: A GitLab-style diff viewer, an Electron password manager, a todo app, an A* solver for the travelling salesman problem and an OpenCV tomato detector.
